findings.summary: Systematic artifact-path divergence: the 14 task contracts name output paths that differ from the downstream graph nodes' required_artifacts and acceptance criteria on 13 of 14 nodes (node-02: decision-schema.md vs decision-schema.json; node-03: sources.md vs sources-inventory.md; node-04: decisions-raw.jsonl vs decisions-raw.json; node-05: decisions-canonical.jsonl vs decisions-normalized.json; node-07: corpus/ vs corpus-snapshot/; node-08: repro-report.md vs repro-check.json; node-10: ingest-report.md vs ingest-receipt.md; node-11: retrieval-check.md vs retrieval-smoke.md; node-15: part1-summary.md vs part1-package/). With artifact_gate_enforced=true, the gate checks the graph paths, so agents following the contracts will produce artifacts the gate rejects — the slice stalls at node-02 and every downstream node. The gddp-config node YAMLs predate the result commit, so the contracts were expected to align with them and did not.

Direct contradiction on the evaluation nodes: graph nodes 12-14 require pre-written query files 04-evaluation/queries/q1.txt..q5.txt (acceptance criterion: queries 'written before asking, not adapted after seeing answers') and per-query result files (q1-factual.md, q2-rationale.md, q3-supersession.md, q4-relationship.md, q5-negative-control.md), while the eval contracts direct agents to choose queries at execution and include stop conditions forbidding pre-written query strings in a query-canon file, and emit combined single-file results (eval-factual-rationale.md etc.). An agent following the contracts violates the graph's required artifacts and its scientific-integrity requirement for the negative control.

Room-boundary divergence for node-09 (khoj-transform): the graph requires the transform at 03-ingestion/output/khoj-corpus/ plus 03-ingestion/output/transform-notes.md, but the contract writes 02-corpus/output/khoj-ready/ and never produces transform-notes.md. The node-10 contract then consumes the 02-corpus path, compounding the divergence from the graph's stage definition (corpus room produces snapshot; ingestion room receives the transform).

AGENTS.md was fully overwritten (146 lines of pre-existing MyAPI/MyAPI-rebuild operating notes replaced by an 82-line Part 1 routing map). This was inherent to the acceptance criteria (AGENTS.md must BE the routing map) and old content survives in git history/README/CLAUDE.md, but it is the one modification of an existing file against the 'no changes to existing files' constraint.

integrity.reasoning:
The scaffold work itself is well-crafted: four rooms with CONTEXT maps (all under 60 lines), 14 task contracts covering all 14 downstream nodes 1:1, internal cross-references that resolve, all referenced repo paths (docs/01-taxonomy.md, deploy_to_khoj.sh, scripts/reindex_khoj_safe.py, project-docs/corpus-work-2026-08/CORPUS-TARGET-SHAPE.md, etc.) verified to exist, verification commands that are machine-checkable, and faithful adherence to the 'no pre-answering' constraint (contracts explicitly decline to prescribe schema fields, source lists, or eval queries). As a standalone scaffold it reads as intent-faithful.

However, the node's intended role is precisely to 'write the instructions every later agent reads' so 'the graph stays a thin scheduler' — and the instructions it wrote systematically contradict the graph's own source of truth. The gddp-config node YAMLs (committed before the result) fix concrete required_artifacts and acceptance paths for every later node; the contracts name different paths for 13 of 14 nodes, put node-09's output in the wrong room, and — worst — the eval contracts actively forbid the pre-written query files that nodes 12-14 require as gate-checked artifacts. With artifact_gate_enforced=true, downstream execution fails at the first gate (node-02 expects decision-schema.md; contract says decision-schema.json). This is not a subtle veer (drift) nor merely unverifiable (insufficient): it is a verifiable, systematic misalignment that actively prevents the slice from executing as designed, so the correct verdict is block with human review before node-02 fires. Lane-1 indeterminate criteria (e.g., 'CONTEXT.md absent' probe artifact) are out of scope here; this verdict rests solely on the contract-vs-graph artifact contradiction.
